content: Alcon is a global medical company that specializes in eye care products. Its corporate headquarters are located in Hünenberg, Switzerland, while its U.S. headquarters is based in Fort Worth, Texas. Alcon was established in 1945 in Fort Worth, Texas, by two pharmacists, Robert Alexander and William Conner. The company was named after its founders, combining parts of their last names. Initially, Alcon operated as a small pharmacy, focusing on sterile ophthalmic products, which were not widely available at the time. The founders prioritized reducing contamination and improving safety in eye care products. After incorporating in 1947, the company experienced steady growth and became a leader in the field of ophthalmology. In 1977, Nestlé, a Swiss multinational corporation, acquired Alcon. This marked Nestlé's first foray into the pharmaceutical industry during a period of rapid expansion. Under Nestlé's ownership, Alcon significantly increased its manufacturing capabilities by establishing new production facilities in South America and Europe. The company also made substantial investments in research and development. By the 1980s and 1990s, Alcon had grown to become the largest and most profitable ophthalmic company globally. Its product portfolio expanded beyond pharmaceuticals to include surgical products, such as the AcrySof intraocular lens implant, which is now the most widely used lens implant in cataract surgeries worldwide. Today, Alcon operates in 75 countries, and its products are sold in over 180 countries. The company employs more than 12,000 people worldwide. In 2002, Alcon was spun off from Nestlé and re-entered the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) with an initial public offering (IPO) on March 21. Despite the spin-off, Nestlé retained 75% ownership of Alcon's stock. Consumer Products Contact Lens Care Opti-Free RepleniSH Multi-Purpose Disinfecting Solution: A solution designed for cleaning, disinfecting, and storing contact lenses. Opti-Free Express No Rub Solution: A no-rub disinfecting solution for contact lenses. Opti-Free Supraclens Active Cleaner: A cleaning solution for contact lenses. Unique-pH Multi-Purpose Solution: A discontinued multi-purpose solution for contact lenses (production ceased in July 2007). Clerz Plus Lens Drops: Drops designed to refresh and rewet contact lenses. PLIAGEL Cleaning Solution: A cleaning solution for contact lenses. ALCON Saline Solution: A saline solution for rinsing contact lenses. UNISOL 4 Saline Solution: A preservative-free saline solution for contact lenses. Dry Eye Products Systane Lubricant Eye Drops: Eye drops designed to provide long-lasting relief for dry eyes. Tears Naturale Forte Lubricant Eye Drops: A formulation for relieving dry eye symptoms. Tears Naturale Lubricant Eye Drops: Eye drops for mild to moderate dry eye symptoms. Tears Naturale II Lubricant Eye Drops: A second-generation formulation for dry eye relief. Bion Tears Lubricant Eye Drops: Eye drops for severe dry eye symptoms. Poly-Tears Lubricating Eye Drops: A lubricating solution for dry eyes. Other Consumer Products ICAPS Vitamins: Eye health supplements designed to support vision and overall eye health. Naphcon-A Eye Allergy Drops: Eye drops formulated to relieve symptoms of eye allergies. Pharmaceutical Products Glaucoma Medications Azopt (brinzolamide): Betoptic (betaxolol): Betoptic S (betaxolol suspension): A suspension formulation of betaxolol for glaucoma treatment. DuoTrav (travoprost/timolol): Iopidine (apraclonidine): Isopto Carbachol (carbachol): A cholinergic agent for glaucoma management. Isopto Carpine (pilocarpine): A miotic agent used to treat glaucoma. Travatan (travoprost): Travatan Z (travoprost): A preservative-free formulation of travoprost. Ocular Antibiotics Ciloxan (ciprofloxacin): An antibiotic for bacterial eye infections. TobraDex (tobramycin/dexamethasone): A combination antibiotic and steroid for treating eye infections and inflammation. Tobrex (tobramycin): An antibiotic for bacterial eye infections. Vigamox (moxifloxacin): A fluoroquinolone antibiotic for bacterial conjunctivitis. Ocular Anti-Inflammatory Agents Flucon/Flarex (fluorometholone): A corticosteroid for treating ocular inflammation. Maxidex (dexamethasone): A corticosteroid for managing eye inflammation. Nevanac (nepafenac): A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) for post-surgical inflammation. Patanol (olopatadine): An antihistamine for allergic conjunctivitis. Vexol (rimexolone): A corticosteroid for ocular inflammation. Otic Antibiotics Ciproxin HC/Cipro HC (ciprofloxacin/hydrocortisone): A combination antibiotic and steroid for ear infections. Ciprodex Otic (ciprofloxacin/dexamethasone): A combination antibiotic and steroid for otic infections. Econopred Plus (prednisolone acetate): A corticosteroid for inflammation. Macular Degeneration Treatment Retaane (anecortave): A treatment for age-related macular degeneration. Surgical Products LADARVision: A laser system used for performing laser eye surgeries. LADAR-6000 Surgical Laser: A surgical laser system for ophthalmic procedures. INFINITI™ Vision System: A system used for phacoemulsification cataract surgeries. Ophthalmic Viscosurgical Devices: Specialized devices used during eye surgeries to maintain space and protect ocular tissues.
